name: HT Media Ltd
title: HT Media Ltd - 532662 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Print ad yields drove a 10% Q4 ad revenue rise and 14% FY26 print margin, while Radio and OTTplay losses were cut by exiting six loss-making frequencies and OTTplay; volumes flat, no numeric guidance.

summary.headline: HT Media Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 5% to INR 131 crore with margin up 100 bps to 23% on ad yields, while radio and OTTplay drag continued.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was flat for FY26 and down 2% in Q4 to INR 558 crore, but EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps both in the quarter and the full year. Print drove the result, with advertising revenue up 10% in Q4 on higher ad yields, while volumes were broadly flat. Radio revenue fell on a high events base, and management surrendered six loss-making radio frequencies and exited the OTTplay subscription business effective 1 April 2026. Net cash remains above INR 1,000 crore, though other income fell about INR 50 crore on mark-to-market losses on treasury holdings.

financial_highlights.change: down from INR 218 crore in FY25 (about INR 50 crore)

segments.name: Print (combined)
segments.commentary: Q4 operating revenue INR 427 crore (up ~8%-level growth stated for FY) with operating EBITDA INR 97 crore at 23% margin; FY26 operating revenue INR 1,500 crore (up 8%), operating EBITDA INR 208 crore (14% margin). Q4 ad revenue INR 313 crore (up 10%); FY ad revenue INR 1,148 crore (up 8%); circulation nearly flat for FY.

segments.name: Print English
segments.commentary: Q4 ad revenue INR 172 crore (up 9%); FY ad revenue INR 644 crore (up 8%). Q4 circulation INR 13 crore (up 13%); FY circulation INR 53 crore (down 5%).

segments.name: Print Hindi
segments.commentary: Q4 ad revenue INR 142 crore (up 12%); FY ad revenue INR 504 crore (up 8%). Q4 circulation INR 38 crore, roughly flat; FY circulation INR 155 crore.

segments.name: Radio
segments.commentary: Q4 operating revenue INR 43 crore with operating EBITDA of negative INR 7 crore; FY revenue INR 140 crore with operating EBITDA of negative INR 22 crore. Revenue fell on high prior-year events base; six loss-making frequencies surrendered to government.

segments.name: Digital (Shine and Mosaic, continuing operations)
segments.commentary: Q4 operating revenue flat at INR 39 crore with EBITDA negative INR 2 crore; FY revenue flat at INR 155 crore with EBITDA negative INR 8 crore (negative 5% margin). OTTplay discontinued and reported as discontinued operations.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal revenue or earnings guidance, per the call's standard practice.

No further closure or exceptional losses expected from discontinuing OTTplay beyond small servicing costs for subscriptions sold up to 31 March 2026, which may run to September 2026 and hit FY27 P&L marginally.
Contract exits on content, ISP and channel partners for OTTplay will involve cash outflows, but management said the P&L impact is marginal.
Core Print to receive continued investment in copies and copy share; some investment to go into Digital, specifically Digicontent Ltd.
Ad yield improvement is hoped to hold at current levels or better, but management would not commit beyond that.
Management said no plans currently to return cash to shareholders; Board prefers investing in core and digital businesses.
capex_capacity: Six loss-making radio frequencies (five current plus one earlier) surrendered to Government of India; remaining frequencies described as profitable.
OTTplay stopped selling new subscriptions from 1 April 2026; existing subscriptions run one to six months.
Copy share gains in selected markets, funded by ad yield gains; copy investment described as a conscious, market-by-market strategy.
AFE (advertising for equity) portfolio: management said it is an active seller of matured and semi-matured assets; new AFE deals are non-cash, paid in ad space.
Investment of INR 22 crore by HMVL in Assetvault Limited (AasaanWill), described as an AFE investment with no cash outflow.
demand_pricing: Print growth was driven by ad yields; volumes were broadly flat in line with industry. Yield gains were across English and Hindi.
Circulation realisation per copy was slightly flat to marginally up; English circulation growth in Q4 (13%) was mainly from copies.
Circulation yields flat YoY; management declined to give market-level numbers, citing competitive sensitivity.
Management flagged rising newsprint costs, a weaker rupee and global supply chain and trade uncertainty as near-term cost pressures, managed through cost discipline.

OTTplay failed to reach unit economics despite content, acquisition and retention changes; telcos' presence made the market difficult. Strategic partner and sale talks did not conclude, and management said there is no residual value.

qa_highlights.question: Ad revenue growth in English and Hindi: volumes or pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly pricing and yield; volumes flat, in line with industry. Management said it is unclear how much of the yield gain is structural.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other operating income rise sharply in HMVL?
qa_highlights.answer: It reflects forfeiture of contractual AFE-related revenue that was not received within the specified period.

qa_highlights.question: Why did HMVL's Print segment revenue for the prior year change by about INR 6 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Pervez Bajan said it is an intersegment revenue elimination for OTTplay advertising in print, reclassified because OTTplay moved to discontinued operations; the amount was written off with a matching PBIT impact.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further exceptional losses from radio or OTTplay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further closure losses are expected. A possible statutory charge from the new labour codes could hit exceptional items.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall about INR 50 crore, and why invest INR 22 crore in Assetvault?
qa_highlights.answer: Mark-to-market losses on treasury holdings as yields rose to record highs; the 10-year is near 7%. Management plans to hold to maturity. Assetvault is an AFE investment with no cash outflow.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ad yield sustainable, and what is the cash plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly sustainable, but competitor reactions are a risk. Management aims to keep deals at or above current levels. The Board is investing the cash pile in core and digital and has no current capital return plan.

risks_watch: Newsprint cost inflation and rupee weakness could erode the print margin gains.
Sustainability of ad yield gains given competitor reactions and copy-share spending trade-offs.
Radio sector pressure despite portfolio cleanup; management will review on a close basis.
Residual OTTplay servicing costs through September 2026 and cash outflows from contract exits.
Possible statutory exceptional charge from the new labour codes.
Other income volatility from treasury mark-to-market as bond yields move.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Print pricing and margin delivery, and candid about the exit from radio and OTTplay. Evasive on specific yields, copy share and cash deployment, citing competitive sensitivity and no forward guidance.
key_quotes: The lever for the growth in revenue is primarily yields, volumes have been by and large flat, which have tracked the industry.
The simple answer is no. But even if you break down the exceptional items in this year, one of the big items which is sitting is consequent to the new labour codes.
This was not a capital-heavy business, so there is no residual value.
We are not holding these assets for the very long term.

adds.what: Six loss-making radio frequencies surrendered to Government of India (capacity reduction, not addition)

growth.why: No formal revenue or earnings guidance given; management cited ad yield gains holding at current levels or better without committing further, and no new capacity is being added (radio frequencies surrendered, OTTplay exited).
